summary_paragraph: A 65-year-old man with a history of primary central nervous system lymphoma and diabetes insipidus was admitted for his 31st cycle of high-dose methotrexate chemotherapy. He tolerated the treatment well, with no acute complications. His methotrexate was cleared appropriately, and leucovorin rescue was initiated as planned. Mild hyponatremia (sodium 130) was noted, likely due to fluid retention from IV therapy and prior desmopressin use; management included temporary reduction in desmopressin dosing. His seizure regimen was reviewed, and Topamax dosing was corrected from 25 mg daily to 50 mg twice daily. He remained neurologically stable, with no seizures or focal deficits. He was discharged home in stable condition with updated medication instructions and plans for follow-up MRI and oncology evaluation.
problems: Primary central nervous system lymphoma, unspecified site, extranodal and solid organ sites
Epilepsy, unspecified, without mention of intractable epilepsy
Osteoarthrosis, localized, not specified whether primary or secondary, pelvic region and thigh
